source: claude-architect-exam-guide (github.com/utkarsh1agarwal) — original questions written against the public CCAR-F blueprint

questions.stem: Your resolution agent occasionally calls process_refund before get_customer has returned a verified identity, even though the system prompt says identity verification is mandatory first. What is the most reliable fix?
options: Rewrite the system prompt in bold, capitalized text
Add a programmatic prerequisite that blocks process_refund until get_customer returns a verified ID
Lower the model's temperature
Add five few-shot examples showing correct ordering
questions.why: — Deterministic ordering guarantees for high-stakes operations (money, identity) need programmatic enforcement, not stronger prompt wording. This is the exam's single most-repeated lesson.

questions.stem: get_account_status and get_account_details have nearly identical one-line descriptions. The agent frequently calls the wrong one for billing questions. What's the most effective first step?
options: Merge the two tools into one
Expand both descriptions with input formats, example queries, and explicit "use this vs. that" boundaries
Add a keyword pre-router in front of the agent
Force tool_choice to a single named tool
questions.why: — Tool description quality is the primary, lowest-effort lever for fixing tool-selection confusion. Always fix descriptions before reaching for few-shot examples or architectural changes.

questions.stem: A lookup for "Utkarsh Agarwal" returns three matching customer records. What should the agent do?
options: Pick the most recently active account
Pick the account with the most orders
Ask the customer for an additional identifier (email, order number, zip code)
Process the request against all three accounts and let the customer confirm afterward
questions.why: — Multiple ambiguous matches should never be resolved heuristically; ask for another identifier to disambiguate safely.

questions.stem: A customer says, "I want to speak to a human right now," about a routine, easily resolvable issue. What should the agent do?
options: Attempt to resolve the issue first, and escalate only if the customer repeats the request
Escalate immediately, honoring the explicit request
Explain why a human isn't necessary and continue autonomously
Ask the customer to describe the issue in more detail before deciding
questions.why: — An explicit request for a human should be honored immediately, not investigated around. Offering to resolve first is correct only when the customer hasn't explicitly demanded escalation.

questions.stem: A case is escalated to a human agent who cannot see the prior conversation. The handoff contains only a ticket number and the words "customer upset." What's missing?
options: A sentiment classification score
A structured summary: customer details, root cause, recommended action
The full unedited transcript
A timestamp of when escalation occurred
questions.why: — A structured handoff (customer details, root cause, recommended action) lets a human act without re-investigating from zero; a sentiment score or bare transcript don't solve that gap.

questions.stem: Your team wants to block any refund over $500 from being auto-approved, regardless of what the model decides. What's the most reliable mechanism?
options: A system prompt clause stating the $500 limit
A pre-call tool-interception hook that blocks process_refund above $500 and redirects to escalation
A few-shot example showing a refund being denied at $501
Reducing max_tokens so large numbers can't be generated
questions.why: — A pre-call tool-interception hook gives a deterministic guarantee. Prompt clauses and few-shot examples are probabilistic and can fail.

questions.stem: Multiple heterogeneous MCP tools return dates in different formats (Unix timestamps, ISO-8601, and localized strings). This is causing the agent to misinterpret order age. What's the best fix?
options: A PostToolUse hook that normalizes all date formats before the model sees them
A system prompt instructing the model to "convert dates carefully"
Removing date fields from tool responses entirely
Asking the customer to always state dates in ISO-8601 format
questions.why: — A PostToolUse hook normalizes heterogeneous data formats before the model reasons over them — a hook problem, not a prompting problem.

questions.stem: A customer has two unrelated concerns in one message: a billing dispute and a shipping delay. What's the best approach?
options: Address only the first concern mentioned and ask the customer to submit the second separately
Decompose into distinct concerns, investigate each with shared context, then synthesize one unified response
Escalate immediately since multi-concern messages are inherently too complex
Pick whichever concern seems more urgent and ignore the other
questions.why: — Multi-concern requests should be decomposed into distinct items, investigated with shared context, then synthesized into one unified response.

questions.stem: Your team currently escalates cases when the model's self-reported confidence score falls below 6/10. First-contact resolution remains far below target, with easy cases escalated and hard cases handled autonomously. What's wrong with this design?
options: The threshold is set too high and should be lowered
Self-reported confidence is poorly calibrated — the model is often confidently wrong on exactly the hardest cases
Confidence scores should be averaged over the whole conversation, not per-turn
The threshold should instead be based on the number of tool calls made
questions.why: — Self-reported model confidence is a poorly calibrated proxy for actual case complexity; it fails precisely on the hardest cases, which is what's happening here.

questions.stem: An MCP tool returns {"isError": true, "message": "Operation failed"} for every kind of failure — timeouts, invalid input, and policy violations alike. What's the problem, and the fix?
options: No problem; isError: true is sufficient signal
The agent can't distinguish retryable from non-retryable failures; add errorCategory and isRetryable fields
Replace isError with an HTTP status code instead
Log the error server-side only, since the agent doesn't need to see it
questions.why: — Generic error responses hide information the agent needs to react correctly. Structured fields (errorCategory, isRetryable) let it distinguish retryable, validation, and business-rule failures.

questions.stem: A new engineer joins the team and doesn't seem to follow the team's established code style, even though it's documented. Investigation shows the conventions live in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md on the tech lead's machine. What's the fix?
options: Ask the new engineer to manually copy the file
Move the conventions to a project-level CLAUDE.md committed to the repo
Repeat the conventions verbally in stand-up each day
Add the conventions to the README instead
questions.why: — User-level CLAUDE.md files are personal and not shared via version control. Team-wide conventions belong in a project-level file.

questions.stem: Testing conventions need to apply to every *.test.tsx file in a large monorepo, regardless of which directory it lives in. What's the most maintainable approach?
options: A CLAUDE.md file in every directory containing tests
A .claude/rules/testing.md file with paths: ["/*.test.tsx"] frontmatter
One giant root CLAUDE.md with a "Testing" section
A skill that must be manually invoked before writing any test
questions.why: — Glob-scoped .claude/rules/ apply based on file path pattern, independent of directory — exactly the "convention tied to file type, not location" problem.

questions.stem: You're building a skill that performs deep dependency tracing and produces very long, noisy output. You don't want this output cluttering the main conversation. Which SKILL.md frontmatter option addresses this?
options: argument-hint
allowed-tools
context: fork
paths
questions.why: — context: fork runs a skill in an isolated sub-agent context so verbose output doesn't pollute the main conversation.

questions.stem: A task involves restructuring a monolithic service into 3 microservices, touching 50+ files, with multiple valid ways to draw service boundaries. What's the right approach?
options: Direct execution, refining the boundary as you go
Plan mode, to explore and design boundaries before committing to changes
A single, extremely detailed upfront prompt specifying every file change
Direct execution, switching to plan mode only if something unexpected comes up
questions.why: — Multi-file architectural decisions with several valid approaches are exactly plan mode's use case — explore and design before committing.

questions.stem: A developer asks Claude to "clean up this data transformation function," and across three attempts, the definition of "cleaned up" varies each time (sometimes renaming variables, sometimes restructuring logic, sometimes both). What's the most effective fix?
options: Repeat the same instruction more forcefully
Provide 2–3 concrete before/after examples that pin down what "cleaned up" means here
Lower max_tokens
Request five attempts and pick the best one manually
questions.why: — Inconsistent interpretation of a prose instruction is fixed with concrete before/after examples, not stronger wording.

questions.stem: A code review surfaces three interacting bugs in a module — fixing bug 1 changes what the correct fix for bug 2 should be. How should this be communicated to Claude?
options: One bug per message, sequentially
All three interacting issues together in one detailed message
Only the most severe bug; let Claude find the rest
A summary count of bugs without describing any of them
questions.why: — Interacting issues need to be described together in one message; sequencing them risks contradictory or wasted fixes.

questions.stem: Before implementing a rate-limiting layer in an unfamiliar service, a developer wants Claude to first surface design questions (burst handling, per-user vs. global limits, failure behavior) rather than jump straight to code. What technique fits best?
options: Test-driven iteration
The interview pattern
Prompt chaining
Direct execution with a longer prompt
questions.why: — The interview pattern surfaces design considerations before implementation — well-suited to unfamiliar domains where not every consideration has been anticipated.

questions.stem: A project-scoped /deploy-checklist command should be available to every developer who clones the repo. Where should it live?
options: .claude/commands/
~/.claude/commands/
CLAUDE.md
.claude/config.json
questions.why: — Project-scoped commands in .claude/commands/ are version-controlled and shared with everyone who clones the repo.

questions.stem: You want Claude to write a test suite, then iteratively improve an implementation based on which tests fail. What should you feed back after each attempt?
options: Only the original instructions, repeated
The actual test failures from that attempt
A new, unrelated set of instructions each time
Nothing — Claude should be able to infer failures without being told
questions.why: — Test-driven iteration works by sharing actual test failures after each attempt, not just the original test suite once.

questions.stem: A developer is unsure whether to use .claude/rules/ or a subdirectory CLAUDE.md for a convention that applies to all files under src/api/. Which favors .claude/rules/?
options: The convention only ever applies within that one directory
The convention needs to apply based on file path patterns that might extend beyond one directory in the future
The convention is short enough to fit in one line
There's no meaningful difference between the two options
questions.why: — .claude/rules/ with glob paths scales to conventions that might extend across directories; a subdirectory CLAUDE.md is bound to one location.

questions.stem: A coordinator decomposes "renewable energy policy trends" into three subtasks, all focused on solar policy in a single country. Each subagent executes its assigned task correctly, but the final report is extremely narrow. Where's the defect?
options: The synthesis agent's summarization quality
The coordinator's task decomposition
The web search agent's query construction
The document analysis agent's relevance filtering
questions.why: — Every subagent executed correctly; the narrow coverage comes from how the coordinator decomposed the topic in the first place.

questions.stem: Which statement about subagent context is correct?
options: Subagents automatically inherit the coordinator's full conversation history
Subagents share memory across invocations by default
Subagents require context to be explicitly included in their invocation prompt
Subagents inherit context if invoked within the same API call
questions.why: — Subagents do not automatically inherit context; it must be explicitly included in their invocation prompt.

questions.stem: A coordinator needs both a web search subagent and a document analysis subagent to run concurrently rather than one after another. How should the coordinator invoke them?
options: Two separate Task tool calls made in two separate coordinator turns
Multiple Task tool calls emitted in a single coordinator response
One combined subagent that does both jobs
Sequential invocation is the only supported pattern
questions.why: — Emitting multiple Task tool calls in a single coordinator response runs subagents concurrently rather than sequentially.

questions.stem: A search subagent times out. What should it report back to the coordinator?
options: An empty result set marked as a success
Structured error context: failure type, what was attempted, any partial results, possible alternatives
A generic "search unavailable" string
Nothing — silently retry indefinitely without reporting
questions.why: — Structured error context (failure type, attempted action, partial results, alternatives) lets the coordinator make an informed recovery decision. Silently succeeding (A) or vague strings (C) hide information; runaway retries (D) risk resource exhaustion without reporting.

questions.stem: The synthesis subagent needs to verify simple facts (dates, names, statistics) very frequently — 85% of verification needs are simple, 15% require deep investigation. Routing every check through the coordinator adds significant latency. What's the best fix?
options: Give the synthesis agent full access to all search tools
Give the synthesis agent one scoped verify_fact tool for the common case; keep coordinator routing for complex cases
Batch all verifications to run at the very end of the pipeline
Remove verification entirely to save time
questions.why: — Giving the synthesis agent one scoped tool for the common, simple case follows least-privilege while avoiding unnecessary coordinator round-trips; the rare complex case still routes through the coordinator.

questions.stem: Two credible sources report different figures for the same statistic. What should the synthesis output do?
options: Use whichever source is more recent, silently
Average the two figures
Preserve both values with source attribution and flag the discrepancy
Omit the statistic entirely
questions.why: — Conflicting credible sources should be preserved with attribution and flagged, never silently reconciled by picking or averaging one value.

questions.stem: A subagent's findings are passed to the synthesis agent as a single block of unstructured prose, and the final report loses track of which claim came from which source. What's the fix?
options: Have the coordinator manually re-attribute claims after the fact
Require subagents to output structured claim-source mappings (claim, excerpt, source, date) that synthesis preserves
Reduce the number of subagents to avoid attribution complexity
Have the synthesis agent guess the most likely source based on writing style
questions.why: — Structured claim-source mappings preserve provenance through synthesis; unstructured prose loses which claim came from which source.

questions.stem: A coordinator's allowedTools list does not include "Task". What happens when it tries to delegate to a subagent?
options: It works normally; Task is always available
It cannot spawn subagents at all
It spawns subagents but without passing context
It falls back to a built-in tool automatically
questions.why: — The Task tool must be in allowedTools for a coordinator to spawn subagents at all.

questions.stem: After a subagent crash mid-run, the coordinator needs to resume without losing prior progress. What's the recommended pattern?
options: Restart the entire pipeline from scratch every time
Each agent exports state to a known location; the coordinator loads a manifest on resume and re-injects it
Rely on the model's memory of the prior session
Manually re-type a summary of progress into the next prompt
questions.why: — Structured state exports plus a coordinator-loaded manifest on resume is the recommended crash-recovery pattern.

questions.stem: A report needs to include findings from sources published a decade apart, describing what appear to be conflicting figures. What should the synthesis output require to avoid misinterpreting a genuine trend as a contradiction?
options: Publication or data-collection dates on each finding
A single averaged figure across all sources
Removal of the older sources entirely
A confidence score attached to the more recent figure only
questions.why: — Publication/collection dates let genuine change over time be distinguished from an apparent contradiction between sources.

questions.stem: A developer needs to find every file matching /*.config.ts across a large repository. Which built-in tool is correct?
options: Grep
Glob
Read
Edit
questions.why: — Glob matches file paths/names by pattern.

questions.stem: A developer needs to find every place in the codebase that calls a specific function by name. Which built-in tool is correct?
options: Grep
Glob
Write
Bash with no arguments
questions.why: — Grep searches file contents, which is what's needed to find function callers.

questions.stem: A connected MCP server exposes a trace_dependencies tool that's meaningfully more capable than manually chaining Grep and Read, but the agent keeps using Grep instead. What's the most likely cause?
options: MCP tools are always deprioritized versus built-ins and this can't be changed
The MCP tool's description doesn't make a strong enough case for its capability relative to the familiar built-in
The MCP server is misconfigured at the network level
Grep needs to be removed from the tool list entirely
questions.why: — A thin MCP tool description loses to a familiar built-in by default; enhancing the description (not removing the built-in) is the fix.

questions.stem: An Edit call fails because the anchor text it's trying to match appears more than once in the file. What's the reliable fallback?
options: Retry Edit with the exact same input
Use Read to load the full file, then Write the corrected version
Use Grep to force a unique match
Skip the edit and ask the user to do it manually
questions.why: — When Edit's anchor text isn't unique, Read + Write is the reliable fallback for a full-file rewrite.

questions.stem: A productivity agent needs credentials for a shared, team-wide MCP server, and the token must never be committed to git. Where should this be configured?
options: ~/.claude.json with the token hardcoded
.mcp.json with ${TOKEN_NAME} environment variable expansion
Directly inside CLAUDE.md
A comment at the top of the relevant source file
questions.why: — Project-scoped .mcp.json with environment-variable expansion keeps credentials out of version control while remaining shared team config.

questions.stem: A developer wants a personal, experimental MCP server that only they use, without affecting teammates. Where should it be configured?
options: .mcp.json in the repo
~/.claude.json
.claude/rules/
A shared team wiki page
questions.why: — ~/.claude.json is the user-scoped location for personal/experimental servers.

questions.stem: After several hours of exploring a large, unfamiliar codebase, Claude starts giving vague answers about "typical patterns" instead of referencing the specific classes it found earlier. What's the most direct fix?
options: Restart with no context
Maintain a scratchpad file recording key findings for the agent to reference
Switch to a different model mid-session
Increase max_tokens
questions.why: — A scratchpad file persisting key findings counters context degradation in long exploration sessions.

questions.stem: A developer wants to build understanding of an unfamiliar codebase efficiently, without reading every file upfront. What's the recommended exploration pattern?
options: Use Read on every file in the repository first
Start with Grep to find entry points, then Read to follow imports and trace flow
Use Bash to cat the entire repo into one context block
Ask the user to describe the codebase verbally instead of exploring it
questions.why: — Starting with Grep for entry points, then Read to follow imports, builds understanding incrementally without reading everything upfront.

questions.stem: A generic tool named process_data is used for three very different jobs: extracting data points, summarizing content, and verifying claims — and the agent frequently uses it incorrectly. After improving the description doesn't fully resolve the confusion, what's the next step on the fix ladder?
options: Add ten few-shot examples immediately, skipping other options
Split process_data into purpose-specific tools: extract_data_points, summarize_content, verify_claim
Remove the tool entirely
Rename it without changing its scope
questions.why: — Splitting an overly generic tool into purpose-specific tools is the next rung on the fix ladder once description improvements alone haven't fully resolved confusion.

questions.stem: A team wants to give a productivity agent both Read/Write/Bash and 15 additional MCP tools for various integrations, all available at once. Recent logs show increasing tool misuse. What's the likely cause and fix?
options: The model needs a larger context window
Too many available tools increases decision complexity and misuse risk; scope tools per task/role instead
Bash should be removed since it's the most dangerous tool
The system prompt needs to list all 18 tools more explicitly
questions.why: — Too many available tools increases selection complexity and misuse; scoping tools per task/role is the fix, not a bigger context window or removing a single tool.

questions.stem: A CI job runs claude "Summarize the diff and flag risky changes" and hangs indefinitely, waiting for input. What's the fix?
options: Add the -p (or --print) flag
Set an environment variable to disable interactivity
Pipe an empty file into the command as a workaround
Add a --ci flag
questions.why: — -p / --print runs Claude Code non-interactively, which is required in automated pipelines. (B and D describe flags/variables that don't exist — a common distractor pattern.)

questions.stem: You want automated PR review findings posted as machine-parseable inline comments. What CLI options should you use?
options: --verbose and --debug
--output-format json combined with --json-schema
--print alone is sufficient
--format text
questions.why: — --output-format json with --json-schema produces machine-parseable structured findings suitable for automated PR comments.

questions.stem: The same Claude Code session that generated a bug fix is also used to review that fix before merge, and subtle logic issues are consistently missed. Why?
options: The context window is too small
The same session retains its generation reasoning, making it less likely to challenge its own prior decisions
--output-format json wasn't set
The model needs more few-shot examples of "good reviews"
questions.why: — A session that generated code retains its own reasoning and is less likely to challenge its own decisions; an independent instance reviews more effectively.

questions.stem: Automated code review is producing a 40% false-positive rate concentrated in one finding category. The prompt already instructs the model to "only report high-confidence issues." What's the most effective next step?
options: Add "be even more careful" to the prompt
Define explicit, categorical criteria for that finding type, and consider temporarily disabling the category while iterating
Lower the sampling temperature
Permanently disable all review categories
questions.why: — Vague instructions like "be conservative" don't meaningfully reduce false positives; explicit categorical criteria do, and temporarily disabling a high-false-positive category protects trust while iterating.

questions.stem: A team wants Claude Code's automated review to avoid duplicate comments across re-runs after new commits are pushed to a PR. What should be included in context on re-runs?
options: Nothing — each run should be fully independent
The prior review's findings, with instructions to report only new or still-unaddressed issues
The full git history of the repository
A count of how many times the PR has been reviewed
questions.why: — Including prior findings and instructing the model to report only new/unaddressed issues avoids duplicate PR comments across re-runs.

questions.stem: A single-pass review across a 15-file PR produces inconsistent depth — some files get thorough feedback, others get superficial comments, and the same pattern is flagged in one file but approved in another. What's the fix?
options: Use a model with a larger context window
Split into per-file local-analysis passes, plus a separate cross-file integration pass
Require developers to submit smaller PRs
Run the same single pass three times and vote on findings
questions.why: — Splitting into per-file passes plus a separate cross-file integration pass avoids the attention dilution causing inconsistent, contradictory findings.

questions.stem: A team wants to reduce API costs on two workflows: (1) a blocking pre-merge check developers wait on, and (2) an overnight technical-debt report. Which should move to the Message Batches API?
options: Both
Only the overnight report; keep the pre-merge check synchronous
Only the pre-merge check
Neither, since batch API doesn't support any CI use case
questions.why: — The Batch API's lack of a latency SLA makes it unsuitable for blocking workflows; it's appropriate only for the latency-tolerant overnight report.

questions.stem: Test generation is producing many low-value, duplicate tests that already exist in the suite. What's the most direct fix?
options: Increase max_tokens for the generation call
Provide existing test files in context, and document testing standards/fixtures in CLAUDE.md
Disable test generation entirely
Ask developers to write all tests manually going forward
questions.why: — Providing existing test files in context and documenting standards/fixtures in CLAUDE.md reduces duplicate, low-value test generation.

questions.stem: A CI review pipeline needs its findings to be reliably parseable by a downstream bot that posts PR comments. Which is the most robust approach?
options: Ask the model nicely in the prompt to "format your response as JSON"
Use --output-format json with a --json-schema to enforce structure
Parse the model's free-text output with regular expressions
Manually reformat the output after each run
questions.why: — Enforced structured output via CLI flags is far more reliable than asking nicely in a prompt or parsing free text with regex.

questions.stem: Documented testing standards live only in a senior engineer's head and aren't written anywhere the CI pipeline's Claude Code invocation can access. What's the fix?
options: Rely on the model's general knowledge of "good tests"
Document testing standards, valuable test criteria, and available fixtures in CLAUDE.md
Ask the senior engineer to review every PR manually instead
Add the standards to a Slack channel pinned message
questions.why: — Documenting standards in CLAUDE.md makes them available to every Claude Code invocation, including CI, instead of living only in one person's head.

questions.stem: An extraction pipeline using tool_use with a strict JSON schema never produces malformed JSON, but sometimes produces line items that don't sum to the stated total. What does this indicate, and what's the fix?
options: The schema itself is broken; add more required fields
This is a semantic error, not a syntax error; add a calculated_total field to compare against stated_total
Switch away from tool_use to plain text JSON
Reduce max_tokens to force shorter output
questions.why: — tool_use with a schema eliminates syntax errors but not semantic ones; comparing a calculated total against the stated total catches this class of mismatch.

questions.stem: You have three separate extraction schemas (invoice, receipt, contract) and don't know the document type in advance, but want to guarantee some structured extraction occurs. Which tool_choice setting is correct?
options: "auto"
"any"
A forced call to one specific schema's tool
Omitting tool_choice
questions.why: — tool_choice: "any" guarantees a tool call happens while still letting the model choose which of several schemas fits.

questions.stem: A required field, purchase_order_number, keeps failing validation because the source document genuinely never contains a PO number anywhere. What should you do?
options: Keep retrying with the same prompt
Make the field nullable/optional instead of required
Fabricate a placeholder value so validation passes
Increase max_tokens and try again
questions.why: — When information is genuinely absent from the source, no amount of retrying will produce it; the field should be nullable instead of required.

questions.stem: A retry is needed because a nested array of line items was incorrectly flattened into a single string on the first extraction attempt. What should the retry prompt include?
options: Only a repeated instruction to "format correctly this time"
The original document, the failed extraction, and the specific validation error describing the flattening problem
A completely different, unrelated example document
Nothing further — the model should self-correct silently
questions.why: — This is a structural, retry-fixable error — the retry needs the specific validation error to correct against.

questions.stem: Two tools have nearly identical descriptions, causing selection confusion, and you've already rewritten both descriptions with clear boundaries — but genuinely ambiguous edge cases still cause mistakes. What's the next lever?
options: 2–4 few-shot examples showing correct selection with reasoning for the ambiguous cases
Force tool_choice to always pick one tool
Merge the tools into one
Increase max_tokens
questions.why: — Once description improvements are exhausted, few-shot examples with reasoning are the next lever for genuinely ambiguous residual cases.

questions.stem: An extraction pipeline reports 97% overall field accuracy. A stakeholder wants to reduce human review before fully trusting this number. What should happen first?
options: Immediately reduce human review across the board, since 97% is high
Validate accuracy broken down by document type and field, since aggregate accuracy can mask segment-level failure
Round the accuracy up to 100% for reporting purposes
Stop measuring accuracy since it's already high enough
questions.why: — Aggregate accuracy can mask segment-level failure; validating by document type and field is required before reducing review.

questions.stem: You want to catch novel extraction error patterns that wouldn't normally be reviewed, since your review process currently only samples low-confidence extractions. What should you add?
options: Stratified random sampling of high-confidence extractions
A rule to never review high-confidence extractions
A fixed weekly quota of 10 reviews regardless of confidence
Removing confidence scoring entirely
questions.why: — Stratified random sampling of high-confidence extractions is specifically designed to catch novel error patterns that a confidence-based review process would otherwise never see.

questions.stem: Your team wants to move a blocking, pre-merge invoice-validation workflow to the Message Batches API to save 50% on cost. Is this appropriate?
options: Yes, always — batch API should be used wherever possible for cost savings
No — batch processing has no latency SLA and can take up to 24 hours, making it unsuitable for a blocking workflow
Yes, as long as custom_id is set correctly
Only if the invoices are small in size
questions.why: — The Batch API's lack of a latency SLA (up to 24 hours) makes it unsuitable for any blocking, pre-merge/pre-approval workflow.

questions.stem: An extraction schema needs to categorize expenses, but the fixed set of categories won't cover every real-world case that will eventually appear. What schema design pattern handles this best?
options: A required category string field with no constraints
An enum field with a defined set of categories plus an "other" value and a category_detail string field
A free-text field parsed later with regular expressions
Omitting the category field entirely
questions.why: — An enum plus "other" and a detail string handles extensibility without over-fitting to a fixed list or silently misclassifying novel cases.

questions.stem: After several extraction pipeline iterations, the team wants to systematically analyze which document patterns most often trigger validation errors or get dismissed as false positives by downstream reviewers. What should be added to each structured finding?
options: A random UUID per finding
A detected_pattern field describing what triggered the finding
A free-text comment box with no structure
Nothing — this requires a separate ML model to analyze
questions.why: — A detected_pattern field enables systematic, aggregate analysis of which patterns trigger errors or get dismissed as false positives over time.
